2. BACKGROUND
The Orlando VA Health Care System (OVAHCS) is required by federal regulation to remove all controlled and non-controlled substances that are expired, recalled, or otherwise determined to be unusable from active stock. These substances must be stored separately until destroyed, reverse distributed, or transferred to a DEA-licensed vendor for destruction, in accordance with 21 CFR Part 1317.
OVAHCS is seeking to expand its current destruction-only capability to include pharmaceutical reverse distribution services for non-controlled substances that would otherwise result in lost manufacturer credit opportunities and incomplete inventory lifecycle control, while maintaining destruction capability for both controlled and non-controlled medications across all OVAHCS sites. The intended outcomes include:
Recovery of financial credit for eligible non-controlled medications that are reverse distributed.
Improved inventory management and reduced waste.
Full lifecycle accountability for all medications.
Strengthened compliance with VA, DEA, and federal requirements.
3. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT
The Government is seeking a contractor licensed by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) to provide flat-fee services to collect, transport, reverse distribute, and/or destroy controlled (Schedules I V) and non-controlled medications at OVAHCS facilities. Fees shall not be calculated as a percentage of credit returns under any circumstances.
3.1 Scope Highlights
The Contractor shall provide:
On-site processing of Schedule I V controlled substances and non-controlled substances (including expired, recalled, due-to-expire, or otherwise unusable medications).
A minimum of four (4) on-site visits per calendar year at the Outpatient Clinics and Orlando VA Medical Center, with additional visits as directed by the COR. Response within ten (10) business days of a COR request.
All shipping instructions, forms, labels, postage, DEA-approved tamper-proof pouches, and boxes required for shipment to the Contractor's central processing facility.
Chain-of-custody documentation, including DEA Form 41 for controlled substances, signed by the Pharmacist, Accountable Officer, and Contractor representative.
Manufacturer return coordination, credit reconciliation, and Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) compliance.
A toll-free (800) number and a web-based service request ordering system.
A web-based reporting portal that captures collection date, site, drug name, formulation/strength, NDC, quantity, manufacturer, estimated return value, actual return value, and status of each reverse distribution pickup.
Initial orientation and training on all applicable reports and web-based systems.
A written Substance Collection Plan and Substance Contingency Plan.
3.2 Applicable Regulatory Framework
The Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including but not limited to:
Controlled Substances Act (CSA)
21 CFR Part 1317 (DEA regulations for disposal of controlled substances)
Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA)
21 CFR (Food & Drugs), 29 CFR (Hazardous Materials), 40 CFR (Environment), 49 CFR (Transportation)
EPA, OSHA, FDA, DEA requirements
41 U.S.C. Chapter 67 (Service Contract Labor Standards)
All applicable VA policies and facility-specific security requirements
